questions.q: What are the four parts of the story for each portfolio project?
options: Problem, approach, result, what you would change
questions.explain: Problem, approach, result and what you would change gives a consistent, honest two-minute story for each project.

questions.q: How should you choose which project to lead with?
options: The one that best fits the job description
questions.explain: Match the project to the role: pipeline for sales operations, Project 3 for executive-facing analyst roles, for example.

questions.q: An interviewer asks whether your projects used real customer data. What is the best answer?
options: Explain honestly that it is a fictional company with illustrative data, built to practice realistic decisions
questions.explain: Honesty protects your credibility. The value of the projects is the decisions and reasoning, not the origin of the data.

questions.q: When sharing your screen in an interview, what is a good practice?
options: Point to the answer first and explain one decision behind it
questions.explain: Showing the answer first then explaining one decision keeps the story clear and avoids reading the screen aloud.

questions.q: Why include "what I would change" in every project story?
options: It shows honest reflection and awareness of limits
It lets you skip the result
questions.explain: Naming one honest improvement shows judgment and growth, and it prepares you for the common question about what you would do differently.
